title: Introduce RBAC drift detector, KMS consumption explainer, and audit fingerprint indexer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need an automated way to detect and explain drift between declared RBAC v2 policy state (policy templates + per-tenant bindings) and observed access patterns in production audit logs, together with a lightweight KMS consumption profile so security teams can identify anomalous key usage or cross-region access. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) rbac-drift-detector: a service that periodically compares the desired policy graph against observed allow/deny events and surfaces candidate drifts with an evidence score; 2) kms-consumption-explainer: a small analyzer that aggregates per-CMK usage (calls, envelopes, wrapped keys) and maps usage to tenant claims and region tags to detect cross-region calls and sudden consumption spikes; 3) audit-fingerprint-indexer: a compact indexer that computes stable fingerprints for audit entries (normalized caller, resource, action, region, timing) to make drift correlation and de-duplication efficient.

What changed (high level): added a new service under services/rbac-observability with CLI for one-off scans and a server mode for scheduled runs; new proto and index schemas in infra/audit-index; a migration that backfills a 7-day audit fingerprint shard for initial scoring; RBAC lint rules extended with a "shadow-observability" annotation to mark policies excluded from drift alarms during staged rollouts; integration tests to validate score heuristics and KMS explainers against synthetic workloads; docs and runbook entries for SOC/Platform teams describing investigation flow and mitigations.

Checklist / rollout plan: - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] runbook draft in docs/runbooks/rbac-drift.md - [x] feature flag gated under feature.observability.rbac_drift (default off) - [x] migration to create audit_fingerprint_shards table (backfill limited to 7 days) - [x] staged rollout to internal infra then canary tenants then wide release - [x] notify SOC and SRE channels and add alert templates for high-confidence drifts

Operational notes: The detector computes an evidence_score (0-100) using weighted signals: unexpected-allow-events, failed-authentication-probes, KMS-region-mismatch, rate-of-change in bindings. The KMS explainer outputs a short human-friendly justification per anomalous key event (example: "CMK arn:... used by service-account:svc-ingest in region eu-west-1, tenant claim shows region=us-east-1 => possible cross-region routing via proxy-operator"). The fingerprint indexer normalizes audit payloads (removes ephemeral request IDs, normalizes caller ids, canonicalizes resource ARNs) and stores a 64-bit fingerprint which is used to group events quickly in the web UI and in the alert payloads.

Migration and data retention: The migration creates a rolling 7-day backfill by default to limit storage and risk; teams can request longer retention via support. The migration is reversible (drops index shards) if rollback triggered. Backfill runs are rate-limited and instrumented to avoid load spikes on the audit store.

Security considerations: The new services run in a restricted operator role with read-only audit-store permissions and explicit deny for key-decrypt operations. We added an operator-bound KMS wrapper to ensure the analyzer never exports raw key material; only metadata (key id, region, usage counters) are stored. All artifacts are covered by existing audit pipelines and the new audit_fingerprint_shards table is encrypted-at-rest and access-controlled via RBAC v2 templates.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on scoring heuristics in detect/heuristics.go and the query plan in infra/audit-index/queries.go for potential performance bottlenecks across large tenants. The CLI provides --simulate to generate synthetic drift scenarios; use it with the canary dataset in infra/testdata/canary-audit.json.

Related: builds on discussions in ENG-6723 and complements earlier residency checks; will be used by SOC playbooks alongside the residency-enforcer gate. If approved, ops will flip feature.observability.rbac_drift on for internal tenants on 2026-03-01 and start canarying tenants with high churn.
commit_summary: 3 commits: (1) initial detector + protobufs; (2) KMS consumption explainer + CLI; (3) migration + tests + docs. Small followups in separate commits adjust heuristics weights after integration test failures.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: The evidence_score composition looks reasonable but I'm concerned about the CPU profile when scanning high-churn tenants. Suggest sampling by tenant and incremental anchors.
Asha Patel: Added a tenant_sampling window and incremental anchor logic in heuristics.go; tests updated to cover sample path.
Rina Sato: Please double-check the KMS explainer does not accidentally log key ARNs in plaintext in debug mode.
Asha Patel: Confirmed; explainer logs only key IDs and region; added unit test to assert no full ARNs are emitted.
Chris Morgan: Integration test failed on first run due to missing migration permissions in CI; bumped migration role in test harness and re-ran. CI green now. Approving for merge.
ci_checks: security-scan: pass (no deps with high CVE severity)
merge_commit_message: squash: add RBAC drift detector, KMS consumption explainer and audit fingerprint indexer\n\nIntroduces observability tooling to detect policy drift and anomalous key usage. Backfill migration for 7-day fingerprint shards. Includes docs and runbooks.
release_notes: Add: RBAC drift detector service, KMS consumption explainer, and audit fingerprint indexer. Feature is feature-flag gated (feature.observability.rbac_drift) and rolled out to internal tenants for canarying. Security: operator role is read-only and migration is rate-limited.
post_merge_actions: Ops to enable feature flag for internal tenant group on 2026-03-01; SOC runbook shared; schedule a follow-up to evaluate false positive rate after 14 days.
notes_for_backport: No backport requested. If backporting to the 2026.02 release, remove migration backfill or run with --skip-backfill to avoid load on older clusters.
